title: Signal graph execution trace
description: A machine-readable trace of one signal-graph run: per node, in execution order, the enforcement tier that ran it, the trust labels of its input and output, and the distinct capability crossings it made (WIT interface + instance name). Sub-graph runs nest. Structure is deterministic across runs of the same graph and input; timing, when present, is an optional field excluded from structural comparison.

graph.description: The name of the graph that ran.

nodes.description: The nodes that ran, in execution order along the taken path.

tier.description: The enforcement tier that ran the node. 'graph' is not an enforcement tier: it marks a sub-graph node, whose body is another graph and whose internal nodes report their own tiers in the nested trace.

input_trust.description: The trust label of the value the node received.

output_trust.description: The trust label of the value the node produced. A node with untrusted input and trusted output has raised trust — a discharge, which the graph requires the node to declare.

crossings.description: The distinct capability crossings the node made, deduplicated by (interface, instance) and emitted sorted. Multiplicity is not recorded: it is a timing fact, and differs between the host and confined tiers for the same node.

subgraph.description: Present only on a sub-graph node: the nested run of the referenced graph, carrying its own nodes' tiers, trust labels, and crossings.

timing_us.description: Optional wall-clock duration of the node's run, in microseconds. Excluded from structural comparison and never populated on the paths the evaluation pins compare, so trace structure stays deterministic.

calls.description: Per-use journal of capability crossings, in encounter order and undeduplicated: the layer replay would need for ordering and multiplicity. The 'crossings' array above is this array's projection (forget operation and index, deduplicate). Deliberately NOT tier-comparable — the host tier calls a capability once where a confined component loops internally under different operation names — so it is absent from the structural form the two tiers are compared on. Confined-tier-authoritative, host-tier-advisory: on the host tier this is exactly as circumventable as every other host-tier guarantee. Values are not captured, so this is not by itself sufficient for replay.

instance.description: The capability instance the crossing landed on.

operation.description: The operation reached for on that capability.

index.description: Position in this node's call sequence, from zero.

interface.description: The capability interface crossed — the WIT interface name where the capability is realised on the confined tier (e.g. aap:caps/tool-llm@0.1.0), or the capability type string for a host-only capability with no WIT interface.

instance.description: The capability instance the crossing landed on: the graph-declared identity label where one exists (making identity routing observable), otherwise the capability's scope.
